chunks: 37 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ghalib from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abd al-Salam ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
"When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see the crescent, break the fast."
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine the start and end of Ramadan fasting based on moon sighting?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the principle of *ru'yah* (visual sighting) as the definitive marker for entering and exiting Ramadan, a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence regarding lunar calendar observance. It highlights the direct link between celestial observation and religious duty, reinforcing the Prophet's tradition that the community's worship is synchronized with the visible phases of the moon. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the Shia view that fasting begins and ends upon actual sighting, rather than purely astronomical calculation, unless specific conditions apply.
